**No — the POOL step is the right step in the right order, but its overload rule as written in NEXT is the wrong one to build.**

**What NEXT prescribes.** Cycle 118's first act is one build step for the pool: `Q_free`/`Q_work`, bound 20, "full ⇒ skip the read" (`STATUS.md:65-66`; `docs/d1-loop12-17-split-plan.md:2171-2172`). It takes that from the queue table: "full `Q_work` ⇒ skip this read, return the slot in the same iteration" (`docs/d1-build-plan.md:572`).

**Why the pool itself is right.** Queueing the single IMAQ refnum would let loop 1.1 overwrite the buffer before 1.2 reads it, so 1.2 could track a different frame (`docs/d1-loop12-17-split-plan.md:2142`). A pre-allocated 20-slot pool is the decided frame handoff (`docs/decisions.md:22`). The input file R2 is accepted (`STATUS.md:64`).

**Why the overload rule is wrong.**
- "Full `Q_work` ⇒ skip this read" keeps the 20 queued old frames and discards the newest one. That is drop-new.
- The decided policy for acquisition → tracking is the opposite: "lossy, latest-wins — discard the backlog, take the newest frame. A stale sample corrupts the time series; an explicit gap does not" (`docs/decisions.md:25`).
- The project's own design document states the user chose latest-wins, "not drop-new" (`docs/frame-ownership-design.md:89-90`).
- The only place drop-new was accepted is `Q_focus`, and that acceptance says explicitly that latest-wins remains the rule for the frame path (`docs/d1-build-plan.md:1121-1122`, `:1174-1176`).
- With a FIFO of depth 20, tracking under overload always works on frames up to 20 reads old — the stale-sample case the decision exists to prevent.

**The complication, which is why this is not a one-line fix.** The same decisions table forbids the obvious latest-wins mechanisms: "No pool eviction, no `Lossy Enqueue Element`, no generation numbers" (`docs/decisions.md:21`), and says "no free slot ⇒ simply do not read this iteration" (`docs/decisions.md:24`). So rows 21/24 and row 25 are only consistent if the backlog is discarded on the consumer side (1.2 drains `Q_work`, returns the older slots to `Q_free`, tracks the newest), or if the depth is small. Neither appears in the pool row of `d1-build-plan.md:572`. The files do not settle which mechanism stands.

NEXT already sends unsettled design choices "BLOCKED to judgement" (`STATUS.md:68`), but it names only O6/O7 and hands the material session "full ⇒ skip" as settled — so the step would be built and saved with the wrong policy baked in.

**What the next cycle should do instead.** Before any LabVIEW launch, an offline judgement step reconciles `decisions.md:21/24/25` with `d1-build-plan.md:572` and writes the overload mechanism into a Pre-decided entry. If the files cannot settle it, it goes to the user's pending-decisions list. The pool's structural parts (20 slots, two queues, `IMAQ Create` route) can be planned offline in parallel, since they do not depend on that answer.

Confidence: high on the contradiction (direct quotes); medium on the best mechanism, which I did not find specified.

VERDICT: change NEXT
NEXT ACT: Offline, settle how the pool realises latest-wins (discard backlog, track newest frame) without violating the camera-free-runs rule, record it as a Pre-decided entry, and only then build the POOL step with that overload policy instead of "full Q_work ⇒ skip this read".
